paragraphs.text: Follow after love; yet desire earnestly spiritual [gifts], but rather that ye may prophesy.
paragraphs.original: Διώκετε τὴν ἀγάπην, ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ πνευματικά, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε.
paragraphs.translit: Diōkete tēn agapēn, zēloute de ta pneumatika, mallon de hina prophēteuēte.

paragraphs.text: For he that speaketh in a tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God; for no man understandeth; but in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ οὐκ ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ ἀλλὰ θεῷ, οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἀκούει, πνεύματι δὲ λαλεῖ μυστήρια·
paragraphs.translit: ho gar lalōn glōssē ouk anthrōpois lalei alla theō, oudeis gar akouei, pneumati de lalei mystēria·

paragraphs.text: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men edification, and exhortation, and consolation.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἀνθρώποις λαλεῖ οἰκοδομὴν καὶ παράκλησιν καὶ παραμυθίαν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de prophēteuōn anthrōpois lalei oikodomēn kai paraklēsin kai paramythian.

paragraphs.text: He that speaketh in a tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.
paragraphs.original: ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ ἑαυτὸν οἰκοδομεῖ· ὁ δὲ προφητεύων ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: ho lalōn glōssē heauton oikodomei· ho de prophēteuōn ekklēsian oikodomei.

paragraphs.text: Now I would have you all speak with tongues, but rather that ye should prophesy: and greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.
paragraphs.original: θέλω δὲ πάντας ὑμᾶς λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, μᾶλλον δὲ ἵνα προφητεύητε· μείζων δὲ ὁ προφητεύων ἢ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσαις, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ διερμηνεύῃ, ἵνα ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβῃ.
paragraphs.translit: thelō de pantas hymas lalein glōssais, mallon de hina prophēteuēte· meizōn de ho prophēteuōn ē ho lalōn glōssais, ektos ei mē diermēneuē, hina hē ekklēsia oikodomēn labē.

paragraphs.text: But now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?
paragraphs.original: Νῦν δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἐὰν ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς γλώσσαις λαλῶν, τί ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσω, ἐὰν μὴ ὑμῖν λαλήσω ἢ ἐν ἀποκαλύψει ἢ ἐν γνώσει ἢ ἐν προφητείᾳ ἢ ἐν διδαχῇ;
paragraphs.translit: Nyn de, adelphoi, ean elthō pros hymas glōssais lalōn, ti hymas ōphelēsō, ean mē hymin lalēsō ē en apokalypsei ē en gnōsei ē en prophēteia ē en didachē;

paragraphs.text: Even things without life, giving a voice, whether pipe or harp, if they give not a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?
paragraphs.original: ὅμως τὰ ἄψυχα φωνὴν διδόντα, εἴτε αὐλὸς εἴτε κιθάρα, ἐὰν διαστολὴν τοῖς φθόγγοις μὴ δῷ, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ αὐλούμενον ἢ τὸ κιθαριζόμενον;
paragraphs.translit: homōs ta apsycha phōnēn didonta, eite aulos eite kithara, ean diastolēn tois phthongois mē dō, pōs gnōsthēsetai to auloumenon ē to kitharizomenon;

paragraphs.text: For if the trumpet give an uncertain voice, who shall prepare himself for war?
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἄδηλον φωνὴν σάλπιγξ δῷ, τίς παρασκευάσεται εἰς πόλεμον;
paragraphs.translit: kai gar ean adēlon phōnēn salpinx dō, tis paraskeuasetai eis polemon;

paragraphs.text: So also ye, unless ye utter by the tongue speech easy to understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye will be speaking into the air.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς διὰ τῆς γλώσσης ἐὰν μὴ εὔσημον λόγον δῶτε, πῶς γνωσθήσεται τὸ λαλούμενον; ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis dia tēs glōssēs ean mē eusēmon logon dōte, pōs gnōsthēsetai to laloumenon; esesthe gar eis aera lalountes.

paragraphs.text: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and no [kind] is without signification.
paragraphs.original: τοσαῦτα εἰ τύχοι γένη φωνῶν εἰσιν ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ οὐδὲν ἄφωνον·
paragraphs.translit: tosauta ei tychoi genē phōnōn eisin en kosmō, kai ouden aphōnon·

paragraphs.text: If then I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be to him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh will be a barbarian unto me.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν μὴ εἰδῶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς φωνῆς, ἔσομαι τῷ λαλοῦντι βάρβαρος καὶ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν ἐμοὶ βάρβαρος.
paragraphs.translit: ean oun mē eidō tēn dynamin tēs phōnēs, esomai tō lalounti barbaros kai ho lalōn en emoi barbaros.

paragraphs.text: So also ye, since ye are zealous of spiritual [gifts], seek that ye may abound unto the edifying of the church.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ἐπεὶ ζηλωταί ἐστε πνευμάτων, πρὸς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τῆς ἐκκλησίας ζητεῖτε ἵνα περισσεύητε.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hymeis, epei zēlōtai este pneumatōn, pros tēn oikodomēn tēs ekklēsias zēteite hina perisseuēte.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore let him that speaketh in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
paragraphs.original: Διὸ ὁ λαλῶν γλώσσῃ προσευχέσθω ἵνα διερμηνεύῃ.
paragraphs.translit: Dio ho lalōn glōssē proseuchesthō hina diermēneuē.

paragraphs.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γὰρ προσεύχωμαι γλώσσῃ, τὸ πνεῦμά μου προσεύχεται, ὁ δὲ νοῦς μου ἄκαρπός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: ean gar proseuchōmai glōssē, to pneuma mou proseuchetai, ho de nous mou akarpos estin.

paragraphs.text: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.
paragraphs.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν; προσεύξομαι τῷ πνεύματι, προσεύξομαι δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ· ψαλῶ τῷ πνεύματι, ψαλῶ δὲ καὶ τῷ νοΐ·
paragraphs.translit: ti oun estin; proseuxomai tō pneumati, proseuxomai de kai tō noi· psalō tō pneumati, psalō de kai tō noi·

paragraphs.text: Else if thou bless with the spirit, how shall he that filleth the place of the unlearned say the Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he knoweth not what thou sayest?
paragraphs.original: ἐπεὶ ἐὰν εὐλογῇς πνεύματι, ὁ ἀναπληρῶν τὸν τόπον τοῦ ἰδιώτου πῶς ἐρεῖ τὸ Ἀμήν ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ; ἐπειδὴ τί λέγεις οὐκ οἶδεν·
paragraphs.translit: epei ean eulogēs pneumati, ho anaplērōn ton topon tou idiōtou pōs erei to Amēn epi tē sē eucharistia; epeidē ti legeis ouk oiden·

paragraphs.text: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.
paragraphs.original: σὺ μὲν γὰρ καλῶς εὐχαριστεῖς, ἀλλʼ ὁ ἕτερος οὐκ οἰκοδομεῖται.
paragraphs.translit: sy men gar kalōs eucharisteis, allʼ ho heteros ouk oikodomeitai.

paragraphs.text: I thank God, I speak with tongues more than you all:
paragraphs.original: εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ, πάντων ὑμῶν μᾶλλον γλώσσαις λαλῶ·
paragraphs.translit: eucharistō tō theō, pantōn hymōn mallon glōssais lalō·

paragraphs.text: howbeit in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ θέλω πέντε λόγους τῷ νοΐ μου λαλῆσαι, ἵνα καὶ ἄλλους κατηχήσω, ἢ μυρίους λόγους ἐν γλώσσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: alla en ekklēsia thelō pente logous tō noi mou lalēsai, hina kai allous katēchēsō, ē myrious logous en glōssē.

paragraphs.text: Brethren, be not children in mind: yet in malice be ye babes, but in mind be men.
paragraphs.original: Ἀδελφοί, μὴ παιδία γίνεσθε ταῖς φρεσίν, ἀλλὰ τῇ κακίᾳ νηπιάζετε, ταῖς δὲ φρεσὶν τέλειοι γίνεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: Adelphoi, mē paidia ginesthe tais phresin, alla tē kakia nēpiazete, tais de phresin teleioi ginesthe.

paragraphs.text: In the law it is written, By men of strange tongues and by the lips of strangers will I speak unto this people; and not even thus will they hear me, saith the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τῷ νόμῳ γέγραπται ὅτι Ἐν ἑτερογλώσσοις καὶ ἐν χείλεσιν ἑτέρων λαλήσω τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ, καὶ οὐδʼ οὕτως εἰσακούσονταί μου, λέγει κύριος.
paragraphs.translit: en tō nomō gegraptai hoti En heteroglōssois kai en cheilesin heterōn lalēsō tō laō toutō, kai oudʼ houtōs eisakousontai mou, legei kyrios.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to the unbelieving: but prophesying [is for a sign], not to the unbelieving, but to them that believe.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε αἱ γλῶσσαι εἰς σημεῖόν εἰσιν οὐ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἀπίστοις, ἡ δὲ προφητεία οὐ τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἀλλὰ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hōste hai glōssai eis sēmeion eisin ou tois pisteuousin alla tois apistois, hē de prophēteia ou tois apistois alla tois pisteuousin.

paragraphs.text: If therefore the whole church be assembled together and all speak with tongues, and there come in men unlearned or unbelieving, will they not say that ye are mad?
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν συνέλθῃ ἡ ἐκκλησία ὅλη ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ πάντες λαλῶσιν γλώσσαις, εἰσέλθωσιν δὲ ἰδιῶται ἢ ἄπιστοι, οὐκ ἐροῦσιν ὅτι μαίνεσθε;
paragraphs.translit: ean oun synelthē hē ekklēsia holē epi to auto kai pantes lalōsin glōssais, eiselthōsin de idiōtai ē apistoi, ouk erousin hoti mainesthe;

paragraphs.text: But if all prophesy, and there come in one unbelieving or unlearned, he is reproved by all, he is judged by all;
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ πάντες προφητεύωσιν, εἰσέλθῃ δέ τις ἄπιστος ἢ ἰδιώτης, ἐλέγχεται ὑπὸ πάντων, ἀνακρίνεται ὑπὸ πάντων,
paragraphs.translit: ean de pantes prophēteuōsin, eiselthē de tis apistos ē idiōtēs, elenchetai hypo pantōn, anakrinetai hypo pantōn,

paragraphs.text: the secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.
paragraphs.original: τὰ κρυπτὰ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ φανερὰ γίνεται, καὶ οὕτως πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον προσκυνήσει τῷ θεῷ, ἀπαγγέλλων ὅτι Ὄντως ὁ θεὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: ta krypta tēs kardias autou phanera ginetai, kai houtōs pesōn epi prosōpon proskynēsei tō theō, apangellōn hoti Ontōs ho theos en hymin estin.

paragraphs.text: What is it then, brethren? When ye come together, each one hath a psalm, hath a teaching, hath a revelation, hath a tongue, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐστιν, ἀδελφοί; ὅταν συνέρχησθε, ἕκαστος ψαλμὸν ἔχει, διδαχὴν ἔχει, ἀποκάλυψιν ἔχει, γλῶσσαν ἔχει, ἑρμηνείαν ἔχει· πάντα πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν γινέσθω.
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun estin, adelphoi; hotan synerchēsthe, hekastos psalmon echei, didachēn echei, apokalypsin echei, glōssan echei, hermēneian echei· panta pros oikodomēn ginesthō.

paragraphs.text: If any man speaketh in a tongue, [let it be] by two, or at the most three, and [that] in turn; and let one interpret:
paragraphs.original: εἴτε γλώσσῃ τις λαλεῖ, κατὰ δύο ἢ τὸ πλεῖστον τρεῖς, καὶ ἀνὰ μέρος, καὶ εἷς διερμηνευέτω·
paragraphs.translit: eite glōssē tis lalei, kata dyo ē to pleiston treis, kai ana meros, kai heis diermēneuetō·

paragraphs.text: but if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ᾖ διερμηνευτής, σιγάτω ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἑαυτῷ δὲ λαλείτω καὶ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ean de mē ē diermēneutēs, sigatō en ekklēsia, heautō de laleitō kai tō theō.

paragraphs.text: And let the prophets speak [by] two or three, and let the others discern.
paragraphs.original: προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι διακρινέτωσαν·
paragraphs.translit: prophētai de dyo ē treis laleitōsan, kai hoi alloi diakrinetōsan·

paragraphs.text: But if a revelation be made to another sitting by, let the first keep silence.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω.
paragraphs.translit: ean de allō apokalyphthē kathēmenō, ho prōtos sigatō.

paragraphs.text: For ye all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be exhorted;
paragraphs.original: δύνασθε γὰρ καθʼ ἕνα πάντες προφητεύειν, ἵνα πάντες μανθάνωσιν καὶ πάντες παρακαλῶνται
paragraphs.translit: dynasthe gar kathʼ hena pantes prophēteuein, hina pantes manthanōsin kai pantes parakalōntai

paragraphs.text: and the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets;
paragraphs.original: (καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται,
paragraphs.translit: (kai pneumata prophētōn prophētais hypotassetai,

paragraphs.text: for God is not [a God] of confusion, but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀκαταστασίας ὁ θεὸς ἀλλὰ εἰρήνης), ὡς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῶν ἁγίων.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin akatastasias ho theos alla eirēnēs), hōs en pasais tais ekklēsiais tōn hagiōn.

paragraphs.text: let the women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but let them be in subjection, as also saith the law.
paragraphs.original: Αἱ γυναῖκες ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις σιγάτωσαν, οὐ γὰρ ἐπιτρέπεται αὐταῖς λαλεῖν· ἀλλὰ ὑποτασσέσθωσαν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ νόμος λέγει.
paragraphs.translit: Hai gynaikes en tais ekklēsiais sigatōsan, ou gar epitrepetai autais lalein· alla hypotassesthōsan, kathōs kai ho nomos legei.

paragraphs.text: And if they would learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home: for it is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τι μαθεῖν θέλουσιν, ἐν οἴκῳ τοὺς ἰδίους ἄνδρας ἐπερωτάτωσαν, αἰσχρὸν γάρ ἐστιν γυναικὶ λαλεῖν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ti mathein thelousin, en oikō tous idious andras eperōtatōsan, aischron gar estin gynaiki lalein en ekklēsia.

paragraphs.text: What? was it from you that the word of God went forth? or came it unto you alone?
paragraphs.original: ἢ ἀφʼ ὑμῶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐξῆλθεν, ἢ εἰς ὑμᾶς μόνους κατήντησεν;
paragraphs.translit: ē aphʼ hymōn ho logos tou theou exēlthen, ē eis hymas monous katēntēsen;

paragraphs.text: If any man thinketh himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him take knowledge of the things which I write unto you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ προφήτης εἶναι ἢ πνευματικός, ἐπιγινωσκέτω ἃ γράφω ὑμῖν ὅτι κυρίου ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: Ei tis dokei prophētēs einai ē pneumatikos, epiginōsketō ha graphō hymin hoti kyriou estin·

paragraphs.text: But if any man is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δέ τις ἀγνοεῖ, ἀγνοεῖται.
paragraphs.translit: ei de tis agnoei, agnoeitai.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, my brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου, ζηλοῦτε τὸ προφητεύειν, καὶ τὸ λαλεῖν μὴ κωλύετε γλώσσαις·
paragraphs.translit: hōste, adelphoi mou, zēloute to prophēteuein, kai to lalein mē kōlyete glōssais·

paragraphs.text: But let all things be done decently and in order.
paragraphs.original: πάντα δὲ εὐσχημόνως καὶ κατὰ τάξιν γινέσθω.
paragraphs.translit: panta de euschēmonōs kai kata taxin ginesthō.
